transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-02 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chu (Redwood SE), Lena Morris (Aurora Head of AI), Tom Alvarez (Aurora Cloud Architect), Priya Singh (Aurora DevOps), Mark Duarte (Product); some speakers auto-labeled as Speaker 6 in the export.

Summary (auto): Quick check-in on onboarding progress, access setup, environment readiness, and preliminary perf tuning. Agreement to run extended-context perf tests and share security package. Several network action items for Aurora.

Topics: Onboarding status, VPC peering, service account roles, perf runs (8k context), KV cache behavior, quantization/cost tradeoffs, next steps and owners.

[00:00] Nina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Ethan, you're on?
[00:06] Ethan: Yep, here. Morning/afternoon all.
[00:08] Lena: Hi, Lena here.
[00:09] Tom: Tom here.
[00:11] Priya: Priya.
[00:14] Mark: Mark, product.
[00:15] Nina: Great. Thanks. Plan for today is a quick status on the onboarding checklist, confirm network access, and then Ethan will walk through the perf tuning notes and we'll align on next steps.

[02:10] Nina: Priya, can you give a quick update on VPC peering? Last week you said the infra ticket was opened.
[02:19] Priya: Yeah, so the ticket's in, network wants the CIDR ranges and the list of IPs for the Redwood egress. I, um, put the contact in the ticket but we need your side to confirm the peering IPs. Also we had a question on whether we do native VPC peering or Transit Gateway — we're leaning TG but could go peering if Redwood recommends it.
[03:05] Ethan: For pilot, VPC peering is simplest and lowest friction. Transit Gateway is fine for scale, but it adds another step. If you want dedicated capacity later, TG can make sense. For the initial pilot, peering should work.
[03:32] Tom: Our security team asked about proxying through a bastion for egress, is that compatible with Redwood's private deployment model?
[03:40] Nina: Yes, we support a couple options. For the Private offering we can accept peered VPC with our control plane talking over that link; bastion is fine for initial data egress but we usually recommend direct peering for lower latency.

[05:00] Speaker 6: There's a note about VPN vs peering, I think — transcribed weird.

[05:20] Lena: On the dataset side, we've started running the initial evals — got about 2k queries through. We're seeing some hallucination on clinical notes summarization, especially with abbreviations.
[05:38] Ethan: Can you paste an example? Often that's prompt constraining and sometimes model choice — did you start with the larger 8k-ctx model or the 2k?
[05:48] Lena: We're on the 2k variant for now. The docs say the 8k experiment might help with context but we wanted to iterate first.
[05:55] Ethan: Okay, two suggestions: 1) run a token-limited prompt template that forces canonical expansion of abbreviations; 2) try a quick run on the 8k variant during the perf tests — sometimes the extra context reduces false summarization.

[07:12] Mark: Cost is a concern, so before we switch to 8k we need expected delta on p95 latency and per-token unit cost.
[07:25] Ethan: Totally. We'll run the perf batch — 8k with intermittent cache hits and cold starts — and quantify p50/p95 and token cost. We'll put numbers in the shared benchmark spreadsheet.

[08:50] Tom: Relatedly, what's Redwood's guidance on quantization and quality regressions? If we go 4-bit quant we'd save cost but worried about subtle clinical errors.
[09:05] Ethan: Good question. For clinical, we recommend starting with FP16 or 8-bit with awareness — Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles matched to your workload. For sensitive outputs, we run A/B evals on a labeled prompt set. If you see regressions we can roll back.

[10:30] Priya: On permissions/setup, we granted a service account but it looks like the role is missing the 'compute.network' permission — our CI can't initiate the peering from our side.
[10:44] Nina: Got it. Priya, can you paste the exact error in the ticket? We'll have our infra team look.
[10:50] Priya: Yeah, will do.

[11:55] Ethan: Quick note on KV cache — your engineering note called it K-V cash in the doc, haha — but the practical thing is, if your queries are repeated per patient, prefix caching will reduce per-token cost a lot. For summaries, repeated template is a win.
[12:15] Lena: We're not consistent on patient-level prefixes in the prompt, that could explain some misses. We'll standardize.

[13:40] Speaker 6: Slight hiccup, someone's audio dropped for a sec.

[14:05] Nina: Security questions we got last round — SOC 2, encryption at rest/symmetric KMS, audit logs. Ethan, do we have the SOC2 doc ready to share?
[14:16] Ethan: Yes, we have the SOC2 summary and the ISO attestation. I'll push the link after the call; Nina will send the pilot contract and pricing.

[15:22] Mark: Also need to confirm data residency — our legal asks that PHI not leave the EU for European patients. Is regional private deployment possible for the pilot?
[15:35] Nina: For the pilot, we can run in our EU region with dedicated tenancy, yes. For strict on-prem requirements we'd move to Private on-prem, but EU hosting should satisfy residency for now.

[17:00] Tom: Can Redwood's audit logs show token-level attribution for requests? Our compliance needs tie logs to user IDs.
[17:12] Ethan: Yes, per-request metadata including request id, model id, routing and token counts are in the audit logs. You can ship them to your SIEM or we can push to an S3 bucket.

[18:40] Priya: For the peering, network asked for the target IP for the Redwood egress. What IP range should we expect?
[18:50] Nina: We'll provide a /29 with static egress IPs for the peered interface. We'll include that in the network appendix we send later today.

[20:05] Lena: Back to perf: we ran a small batch on the 2k model and p95 was ~420ms with cold starts; p50's okay but p95 spikes. Wondering if batching or reduced beam size could help.
[20:20] Ethan: For those patterns, continuous batching and warm workers help. For cold-start-heavy workloads, burst capacity or pinned instances reduce p95. If you're okay with slightly higher baseline cost, reserved (dedicated) capacity yields more predictable p95.

[22:10] Mark: What are the tradeoffs—hosted vs dedicated for the pilot? Budget-wise we wanted hosted to avoid commitments.
[22:20] Nina: Hosted is easiest and cheaper short-term. Dedicated gives lower variance and predictable latencies for production. For pilot it's common to start hosted, run benchmarks, then shift to dedicated if you need SLA.

[24:00] Tom: How long to spin up dedicated capacity?
[24:05] Ethan: Typically 2–5 business days once contract and capacity are provisioned. For larger GPU footprints it can be a bit longer.

[25:30] Priya: One more question — CI/CD: we want to automate model rollouts via your API. Are there webhooks or a rollback mechanism?
[25:44] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can trigger rollouts via API and get webhook callbacks for deploy status.

[27:20] Lena: Any notes on prompt evals — we want to run quality monitoring automatically.
[27:30] Ethan: We can instrument evals against your golden set and send regression alerts. Redwood Optimize will surface regressions tied to specific prompt test sets.

[29:00] Nina: Okay let's lock action items — Ethan will run the perf test with 8k context and share the spreadsheet. Priya will supply VPC details and we'll send the SOC2 link.

[29:25] Ethan: I'll run tests with both cold/warm and with prefix cache enabled vs disabled. We'll include p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens.

[30:10] Tom: For the perf tests, please simulate patient-level interactions with varying session lengths — some sessions are 1–2k tokens, some go to 6–7k, so mix is important.

[31:00] Ethan: Good call — we'll set up a mixed workload: 60% short, 30% mid, 10% long. We'll include key metrics.

[32:20] Mark: Anything else on security — SAML SSO? We use Okta.
[32:28] Nina: We support Okta SAML; I'll include the SSO setup doc.

[33:40] Priya: One operational note — our staging environment has strict egress rules; how do you recommend we test without wide open egress?
[33:50] Ethan: Use a pinned peering or IP allowlist. For short-term we can also do a tunnel from a bastion host to run smoke tests. But peering is the long-term approach.

[35:00] Lena: On the hallucination issue, could we get a small A/B with temperature and system prompt changes before switching models?
[35:10] Ethan: Yes, we'll run parameter sweeps as part of the perf/quality runs. We'll include temp 0.0, 0.2, 0.5 and compare ROUGE/precision on the labeled set.

[36:45] Speaker 6: minor crosstalk here, two people talking about scheduling.

[37:05] Nina: Scheduling note — propose the infra walkthrough next Tuesday 2026-09-08 at 15:00 CET. Does that work?
[37:14] Tom: Works for us.

[38:20] Nina: Okay, last piece — pricing. For pilot we can provide a short-term hosted promo rate and then tier up as needed. I'll send sample invoice and pricing tiers.

[39:00] Mark: We'll need an estimate for projected monthly spend if 1M tokens/day with 20% long-context calls.

[39:15] Nina: We'll model that in the pricing doc and call out buffering and cache savings.

[40:30] Priya: I'll follow up in the ticket with the exact IAM error and attach network ACL screenshots.

[41:10] Ethan: One last technical note — for high throughput, consider enabling prefix KV cache and increasing worker pool size; we'll include recommended autoscaling policy in the spreadsheet.

[42:00] Lena: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.

[42:05] Nina: Thanks all. We'll share links and action items after this call.

Recap (auto):
- Priya to provide VPC peering details and IAM error logs.
- Ethan to run extended perf tests (8k context + mixed workload) and share results.
- Nina to send SOC2/security docs and pilot pricing.
- Schedule infra walkthrough for 2026-09-08.
